name: XCWF Championship
epitaph: Crowned in a sixteen-man Royal Rumble on Total HaVok, the fed's own debut show under its new name, when Da Masta outlasted the field. It changed hands thirteen more times across the fed's own life — twice to Al Magz, twice to Kamikazi, twice to Royce Mathers, twice to Mark Estep, twice to Zac Moore — and once by fiat, handed from Kamikazi to Al Magz in Fayetteville rather than lost in a ring. Menace was still holding it when the surviving record ends.

name: XCWF Extreme Championship
epitaph: Born at ResurreXtion in a four-way ladder match that opened with three men colliding in midair before it even properly started, and closed with Freak climbing past a tornado DDT'd Justin Pearce to unhook the belt. It is the fed's own richest lineage — twenty reigns in eleven months, three of them changing hands in a single week between Bayamon and Cancun, and three more on one Cancun night alone. Royce Mathers was its last champion the ledger records, crowned in Richmond in July 2002.

name: XCWF Women's Championship
epitaph: Won first by Victoria Vengeance in Chicago in December 2001, and defended seven times across the fed's own women's division. Tessa Windsor and Tasha Evans traded it twice apiece in a single month that summer, and Tessa Windsor was the last champion the ledger records.

name: XCWF Tag Team Championships
epitaph: Held first by the Immature Playaz and defended, vacated and re-vacated across thirteen reigns — a team named Total HaVok shares its own name with the fed's March pay-per-view, a Tag Team Turmoil Match crowned Shannon York and Unfitt Survivor after the belts went dark, and Predator once held them as a solo champion after beating Donovan Simmons in the straps' own first singles defense. Big 'N' Bad were the fed's last champions the ledger records, having already held the belts once before that summer.

name: XCWF United States Championship
notes: The XCWF InterUnited Championship's own title-history page names this belt as one of the two it unified — but its own last recorded champion, Rage (won 26 May 2002), is not the InterUnited belt's own first champion, Menace, and the ledger records no reign between them. The unification fact stands; how this belt's own lineage actually reached it does not.
epitaph: Won first by Mark Massacre in Ames, Iowa, and changed hands nine times — once, in Nashville, the same night twice over, when Al Magz handed it to Freak and won it back before the night was through. Al Magz beat Sumo for it in a hardcore brawl at ResurreXtion; Stryder won the vacant belt from Ninja at Desperation on a Raven Storm run-in. Rage was its last champion the ledger records; the belt was later folded into the InterUnited Championship, though the ledger does not show how it got there from him.

name: XCWF Junior Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Born at ResurreXtion, where Lil Guido beat Jake Simmons with the Bullet to become the first champion. Shawn Boyd and Colby Newsome traded it three times in five spring weeks in 2002, and Talus won it vacant in Indianapolis, the last champion the ledger records.

name: XCWF Intercontinental Championship

events.title: xcwf-interunited
events.note: Menace, Intercontinental Champion since 28 April 2002, won the InterUnited Championship's own inaugural match on this date; the InterUnited title-history page names its own first match a unification bout, and this is the reign that carries forward.

epitaph: Won first by Da Masta on Total HaVok, and carried by Mimic into a two-out-of-three-falls ladder match at Desperation that Kamikazi took in the deciding fall after a masked ally shoved the champion from the ladder. Menace won it in a tournament final in Cancun and carried it into the InterUnited Championship's own creation two months later; PTC's own dated profile of the fed names a different Intercontinental Champion for the week before that, a disagreement the surviving record does not resolve.

name: XCWF InterUnited Championship
epitaph: Created to unify the United States and Intercontinental Championships, won first by Menace in a match the ledger's own key calls a unification bout against Brian Arson. Al Magz took it from him in Indianapolis on the fed's own last recorded show date.

name: XCWF N.E.W. Championship
epitaph: A single reign survives in the ledger: Shawn Kain won the title vacant in Indianapolis on 25 August 2002, the last date the surviving record carries for the fed at all.
